- **R4-M156 G161, A5's part of SPEC 6.3.4's completion rule: a raw Place borrow's Loan is its fresh anchor's, and the result is live
  after a Return** (2026-10-30; the R4 planning session's design `r4-notes\g161\design.md` revision 3, design review 3 ACCEPT; Major,
  two commits, (1) before (2)) SPEC 5.2.2, 15.6.2, 15.6.3, 5.2.1, 5.7, 6.3.4, 16.2.2, 16.2.3.
  - (1) The raw anchor. A Loan whose Place passes a raw Deref is a raw Place borrow's: its referent is a fresh anchor that "recovers no
    owner or Loan" and is not compared with Places not derived from it (SPEC 5.2.2, 15.6.2's table). `MirBorrows.Loans` publishes it
    (`Anchored`) and `Hits` lets no access of any kind reach it; the shallow kinds' stop at a raw Deref past the access becomes part of
    that rule (its clause is deleted). Supersedes design A3 §5's "raw-anchored chains compare only through the same raw Deref" and the
    deep kinds' within(X, A) across a raw Deref that `Hits` kept from A3's step comparison (E3, R4-M66): the reason to compare a raw
    borrow's Loan with the pointer's holder, that the Loan sits on the holder's path, does not hold under 5.2.2, where the anchor starts a
    path of its own and a `uniq` raw borrow's exclusivity "rests on this promise alone" (a read or a second raw borrow through the same
    pointer is an unsafe obligation). Reading (design review 3, N4): 5.2.2's anchor governs every raw Place borrow's Loan, `during self`
    storage and object payloads included, while what the pointer addresses and its authority stay 5.7's and 5.2.1 condition 3's, so where
    a conflict came only from the raw hit the own-step Warning stays. Places derived from the anchor (reached through the borrow's
    result) and parent Loans of a Reborrow through a reference reached by a raw pointer stay checked. It removes MIR-only false errors at
    a Move, an exclusive or shared borrow, an activation and an observing destruction of the pointer's holder, a read and a second raw
    borrow through the same pointer; the old path accepted each.
  - (2) The delivery. A Return delivers local 0 to its caller, which uses it (SPEC 16.2.2 step 5, 16.2.3; a constructor's object is
    built in the storage its caller's construction expression made, 6.3.2-6.3.4), so local 0's holder is live after the Return: the
    exit's fact, which `IMirFlow.Entry`'s contract puts in the Return terminator's block (`MirBorrows.Liveness`); a diverging exit
    delivers nothing. The Return stays a Move of local 0 that takes no value (R4-M66): its check set's Based pass now reads the delivered
    value, so every reader of a live holder counts it. The Loan check meets a Loan rooted at local 0 by the Move row, which is SPEC
    6.3.4's "Field borrows end before completion" at the delivery (15.6.3: Moving a prefix of a live child's path; 15.6's holders, so a
    part overwritten later still carries it); the own-step departures give 5.2.1 condition 3's Warning for a pointer formed through a
    part's own step (the delivery ends the receiver as the constructor's holder, an ancestor with no dereference between); rule W reads
    local 0's escape slot, so its marker decides `Kept`. How an operand Move compares: for Loans it counts its own value (the Valued
    pass) whatever its destination, and own-step departures count it only through its destination live after the Move (Stored); the
    delivery's value is counted by both as a live holder's (Based). Rejected: the Return's Move taking its value (`TakesValue`, the
    observing destruction's class, which own-step departures do not count) or an operand's class (Valued: an operand the MIR does not
    publish, a second Move representation; own steps count Valued only for an activation); the builder giving the Return an operand
    (Full, unneeded); a check at the exit request's FakeRead (before Scope Exit; design review 1). The delivery's records carry their
    Anchor and no witness (DIAGNOSTICS); an early `return`'s record lies at the constructor's declaration (an open issue).
  - Cost (the G258 host over the 122 census programs: the library, the milestones, the MIR goldens and the accepted SPEC variants; A
    dev 4f57b57f4, A' its byte copy, B 0470ceaee, from one folder, interleaved with the side order rotated, 3 runs x 8 reps, CPU 2
    pinned, tiering off; sums of per-program medians): A5's step 4 B/A 0.991, A'/A 0.988, B/A' 1.004 (minima 0.992, 0.989, 1.002), step 2
    B/A' 1.003; Work 12,254,995, Bytes 268,904 and the 7 problems equal on every side, and so are cold step 4 (87,463,456 B), warm step 4
    (3,424 B) and warm step 2 (3,622,752 B). Bind on Hello and Milestone26 (3 runs x 20 reps): cold B/A 0.995 and 0.995 (A'/A 0.999 and
    0.997), warm 0.993 and 0.997; cold allocation equal (4,858,160 and 4,932,944 B), warm 0 B.
- **R4-M157 G307, A5's Type walks visit a DAG of Types once per Type: a stored part's inline parts keyed by what their facts read**
  (2026-10-30; the R4 planning session's design `r4-notes\g307\design.md` revision 3, joint design review 3 ACCEPT by R4's reviewer and
  review 2 ACCEPT by BU's; Major; the Binding part, `TyCtxt.WrittenAt`, is BU-58) V16 (PLAN G307).
  - Cause: `MirTypes.Holding.Holds` skipped its memo for an inline Tuple or fixed array of a stored part, since a raw layer there reads
    its step by its positions (`TyCtxt.RawStep`, `RawMembers`), and so walked every position: on bu69's family `D_i<T> { x: D_{i+1}<(T,
    T)> }` 2.8 k to 201 M visits from n = 8 to 26 for 348 queries; `MirBorrows.Addresses`' `Inline` (Layering's test, 336 M at n = 26)
    and `Encloses` (25 M on raw leaves at n = 24) had the same shape. From G2 the default check runs them.
  - Rule: a raw layer's step and members read the kept layer (the walk's node), the Type the declaration writes at its position
    (`TyCtxt.WrittenAt`) and the instance; the positions add nothing beyond the written Type, which follows them. The holding memo's key,
    `MirHoldingKey (Type, Stored, Written, Holder)`, is what a part's facts read: (K, false, null, null) for any part outside a stored
    part's inline positions; (K, true, null, null) for an inline Tuple or fixed array of a stored part where `WrittenAt` is null; (K,
    true, W, I) where it is not. Premises, BU-58's contract, both clauses: the facts at or below a node are a function of (K, W, I),
    and W below follows from W; where W is null no layer at or below steps Own or Shared and none appends a member, which the key's
    second shape and `Encloses`' null exit both rest on.
  - Holding: one key path (memo lookup, `Meet` past the bound, the LoanOnly rule, `Enter`), `WrittenAt` asked only at a part's first
    positions and below a non-null W (`asks`), a stored part's root keyed, and an enum Case's payload components its part's first
    positions: its payload Tuple is Binding's and no key, since one kept payload can stand for Cases written differently (E3:
    `A(raw/(ref/i32 during s) during s, i32)` beside `B(raw/(ref/i32 during static) during static, i32)`, one interned payload at `E3
    during static`). Deleted: the per-position walk and "an inline Tuple or fixed array, whose positions decide it, gives them at once".
  - Past the bound: an inline part of a stored part gives the bound's facts (Loan in its own storage, Deep where the mode reads the
    write fact) only where its key is never entered within the bound, R4-M153's per-Type rule on the key. That changes tracking and the
    guard (`D<(W, N30)>`, W = ((i32, i32), (i32, i32)) at depth 2 and 32: holds true and Deep became false and None) and restores the
    order independence R4-M153 states, which the "at once" broke (`D<(N30(S), S)>` gave (true, Deep), `D<(S, N30(S))>` (false, None);
    both now (false, None)).
  - Addresses: one scratch set of visited (Type, written Type); `Inline` visits each Type once per pre-pass; `Encloses` is false at a
    null W, else visits each (Type, W) once per enclosing use; each visit of either is a step of `Work` (A3 6.2), which counted one per
    row before.
  - Supersedes in part: R4-M120's "a raw layer and its part's inline Tuples bypass the per-(Type, mode) memo" (a raw layer is read at
    each meeting of its keyed parent) and R4-M153's "The holding walk keys its slots by Type with one per mode".
  - Rejected: keying below the region by the instance (one shared part walked per instance: `All64<T_20>` 1,280 keys against 20; design
    review 2's B3); an unkeyed stored-part root (keeps the order dependence past the bound); a key on an enum Case's payload Tuple (E3
    answers None where Through); a per-position walk bounded by the declaration's text (a closed associated projection writes a 2^n
    DAG, BU's review 1); a width budget or a Resource record (refuses valid programs a linear walk decides).
  - Tests: TypeDagScalingTest's Holding rows (raw leaves below the region at T_30, the key set of `D<T_40>`, the Stored bit, the written
    twins Q2 and Q3, the holder twin SP (`(SP<i32>, SP<B>)` in both orders, one written part whose `during self` layer reads each
    instance's Type argument), E3, the past-bound and order rows, one Type stored by 64 instances, the projection chain; its raw-leaf
    rows at n = 30 are Explicit until G309) and MirBorrowsTest's `TheAddressWalksVisitATypeDagOncePerWalk`; each fails first on dev
    (its exponential walk, or the changed answers), and each key component has a row that fails without it.
  - Measured. Visits on the family (348 queries, n = 8 / 24): Holds 1,260 / 1,746 (tuple; dev 2,781 / 50.3 M) and 1,081 / 1,257 (raw
    leaves, 26 `RawStep` calls; dev 1,648 / 33.6 M, 8.4 M), Layering's `Inline` 117 / 277 (dev 1,731 / 83.9 M), `Encloses` 3 (dev 381 /
    25.2 M). Cost (the G258 host over the 122 census programs, A 4555482e8 = dev 3e614b427 with BU-58's (b), A' its byte copy, B A with
    this unit, from one folder, interleaved with the side order rotated, 3 runs x 8 reps, CPU 2 pinned, tiering off, a loaded machine;
    sums of per-program medians): A5's step 4 B/A 0.998, A'/A 0.996, B/A' 1.003 (minima 0.999, 0.995, 1.004), step 2 B/A 1.000; Work
    12,254,995 to 12,261,128 (the address walks' visits, +49 a program), Bytes 268,904 and the 7 problems equal; cold step 4 +48,584 B
    over the 122 programs (the visited set and the larger key), retained +376 B a program, warm step 2 and step 4 unchanged. Bind on
    Hello and Milestone26 (3 runs x 20 reps): cold B/A 1.000 and 0.996 (A'/A 1.007 and 1.006), warm 0.998 and 0.999; allocation equal,
    warm 0 B.
  - Open: `Encloses` costs O(distinct (Type, W) of the Place's Type) per use; a per-Place memo, as `ownAt` has, would make it per
    distinct Place (design review 1's N4).
- **R4-M158 G305, the backward dataflow is the forward one's transpose: a value used on a Never form's assumed continuation is live
  before the form** (2026-10-30; the R4 planning session's design `r4-notes\g305\design.md` Option 1; Major; the owner, asked whether
  R4-M34's backward clause may be superseded and the two MirDataflowTest expectations changed, answered 「Okです」 (2026-10-30,
  verbatim)) SPEC 14.10.3, 15.6, 15.6.7 (PLAN G305).
  - Cause: `us[take(x@move)] = x@ref`, `take` of Type Never, was accepted on every pipeline. The MIR is right: the Never call's
    CheckTarget starts the assumed continuation, which uses the secured `x@ref` (SPEC 13.7.1 step 1). A5's holder liveness
    (`MirDataflow.Backward`) let a P1 chain join only its runtime successors, so a use on the continuation kept nothing live at the
    Move, and let a P2 chain join every successor, so a use after a P1 join kept a Loan live on a continuation flowing into the join
    (`if c` { `take("t")`; `consume(x@move)` }; `use(r)`: a MIR-only false error). The backward edges were not the forward ones
    reversed.
  - Rule: one edge rule, `MirDataflow.Flows`: a state flows from chain h along edge i into head s where s is P2, or h is P1 and i a
    runtime edge (SPEC 14.10.3: an assumed continuation continues from its Never form's state, where every check applies; an item with
    a real incoming path uses only real paths). `Forward`'s phase solve and `Backward`'s `Unwind` both read it; the phase solve keeps
    its frozen-P1 shortcut. Every Never form of 14.10.3 shares it (a Never call, also in a `defer`, `$abort`, a transfer, `loop`
    without exit, a diverging operand), and so does every check that reads holder liveness: Loan conflicts and reservations (`k.bump(lose(k@move))`:
    `CallReservationConflict_Kd`). A Drop on an assumed continuation observes like any other cleanup (SPEC 14.10.3: "Cleanup is
    checked the same way"; 15.6.6: what destruction may observe must be valid there; its access is R4-M57's one rule `Dropping`,
    `Observe` where its case Type observes and its A2 group's verdict is not Elide, no group: the case Type alone; R4-M33 superseded
    R4-M24's "observes nothing"), so `Flows` now also keeps a Loan such a Drop observes live before the Never form:
    `let g = Guard.init(x@ref)`, `g`'s Type with a `drop`, then `x = "z"` before `take("t")` or inside a `loop` without exit, is an
    error at the write (it was valid on A5). A4's effect rule (R4-M6a, `MirEffects.Dropped`: a Drop only the checks reach runs no destructor) is
    unchanged: it concerns what runs.
  - Supersedes R4-M34's backward clause ("a P1 chain's runtime successors only and a P2 chain's every successor"). Its reason, "uses on
    continuations never merge into runtime paths", holds for P1 heads, not for a P2 continuation, which by SPEC 14.10.3 continues from
    its P1 predecessor's state.
  - Rejected: joining every successor in both phases (false errors where a transfer's continuation flows into a P1 join, and keeps the
    false error above); a builder use of the secured operands before each diverging terminator (a clause per form, missing uses in
    later statements, the two directions still disagreeing); a forward set of invalidated Loans checked at the use on the continuation
    (a second conflict mechanism for one rule).
  - Tests (each changed expectation SPEC-required and owner-approved): `MirDataflowTest`'s reference rule is the transpose;
    `CheckOnlyUsesKeepNothingLiveOnRuntimePaths` became `ValuesStayLiveIntoACheckOnlyContinuation` (x read after a `return` is live at
    the entry; x read after a conditional `return` is live in no block only the checks reach); `MirBorrowsTest`'s
    `ALoanStaysLiveIntoANeverFormsContinuation` (each Never form above, `defer` and the observing Drop included, an error at its
    reachable twin's location; valid counterparts, a holder without a `drop` and one moved away before the write among them).
  - Old path: such forms without an unreachable local use stay accepted until R6-check (STATUS, Unreachable code).
- **Owner decisions, only when triggered:** O1 a MIR vocabulary member or `IntrinsicId`; O2 a total cap above 142,000;
  O3 an acceptance change outside plan Appendix B (C1–C6 and X1–X3 with a SPEC clause; T1–T4 belong to R7), any rejection
  of a milestone or library program, or a row reopening a SETTLED entry; O4 a general SPEC rule left Unsupported at the R4
  exit; O5 the unclassified count failing to fall in two sessions in a row (plan §18 P9; superseded by R4-M35).

## Language changes (2026-10-16)

- **PR-1 Place results removed; a subscript follows its selected call's reference** (2026-10-16, planning session; owner
  approved the removal, its timing before R6 and the D5 exception for it; proposal
  [Place Result Removal](../../draft/Changes/2026-10-16%20Place%20Result%20Removal.md), two independent designs compared in
  its 2026-10-15 edition).
  - Adopted: a function result is a Type (SPEC 7.1). `index` returns `ref/Element during self` and `indexUniq`
    `uniq/Element during self`; `receiver[key]` through a conformance designates the referent of the reference the
    selected call returns (SPEC 4.7.1), and a written `index`/`indexUniq` call is an ordinary call returning that
    reference. Every call publishes its plan's result Type; the subscript owner (`Binding.Indexers`, `Binding.Views`)
    types the element once from the selected call's plan (`LentElement`) and publishes it on the subscript, HIR
    `HirPlaceKind.CallResult` has that one producer, and MIR `Referent` reads the selected plan.
  - Deleted: `FunctionResultMode`, `BoundType.ResultMode` and its interning, identity, relation and pass-through sites,
    `CallPlan.ResultMode`, `ResultModeOf`, `PlaceExpected`, `CheckPlaceResultOperand`; `PlaceResultKoto`,
    `KotoKind.PlaceResult`, `SyntaxForm.PlaceResultSuffix` and the `place` contextual keyword; `BindingFailure.PlaceRequired`,
    `PlaceRequired_Kd` and their requirement entries; `ExpectedAdaptationKind.ExclusiveBorrow` (Place publishing only;
    `HirAdaptation.ExclusiveBorrow` stays); the result-mode filters of identification, overrides, closures and Callable fits
    and the Place exclusion of associated-Type evidence; Binding's general Place-call branches, the old paths' general
    Place-call branches (`ReferenceTemporary`, the unacquired Place statement, writes and updates through a Place call)
    and the MIR result-temp branch.
  - Rejected: keeping Place results with a shared Follow inside their owners (result modes stay in Callable, matching and
    inference); Place results only for the index requirements, or as compatibility syntax (+100 tokens; modes stay in
    function Types, CallPlan and matching); `CallPlan.ResultMode` kept for synthesized index calls (the two Types and the
    MIR branch stay); Place results as sugar for a reference plus an implicit Follow at every call position; implicit
    Follow of every reference result (`let r = f()` must keep the reference, SPEC 3.3.3, 3.6); subscripts as ordinary
    calls followed by the user (breaks SPEC 4.7.2 parity); a synthesized Follow node or Deref publication per subscript
    (selection happens after binding and capability comes from the receiver path: two forms of one concept). SETTLED
    records the language-level ones.
  - Timing: the proposal defaulted to after R6; R4 paused, the owner chose to land it now with a D5 exception limited to
    deleting Place-only branches and keying the old paths' subscript branches on the selected call. No temporary
    structure was needed: the old paths recognize the selected call (`ElementAccess.IsIndexerCall`) and read the element the
    subscript publishes (`ElementAccess.DesignatedType`), which goes with them at R6.
  - Earlier reason that no longer holds: the 2026-09-25 Shared Place Results proposal compared Place results with a value result
    whose Move is forbidden, not with a reference result that the index expression follows; the caller's choice it wanted
    (Copy, borrow or replace, as for Array) is what following the returned reference gives, and its §7 had already fixed
    the ABI to that of the reference result.

## Diagnostic publication (2026-10-23)

- **G89-1 Override and match facts** (planning session; the owner's G89 request, two independent designs and independent
  design review). SPEC 6.4 and 14.8 keep their existing judgments; SPEC 23.1 and DIAGNOSTICS require retained facts and an
  explanation owned by the diagnostic adapter. `Binding.Diagnostics.VirtualOverrides` and `Binding.Diagnostics.Match`
  own their conversions; the semantic failure records never select wording or repeat a check during publication.
  - First extract the conversions with every published fact, Note, Label and location unchanged. The existing string
    override cause is removed by the following G89 behavior unit, which records cause, compared Types or names, the
    violating parameter's declaration index, proof and locations. Match retains its existing reason and Case index.
  - Rejected: leaving publication in semantic owners, or moving individual cause formatting into DiagnosticOwner.
    The existing phase-specific adapters own these conversions; the common owner keeps schema and display limits.

- **G89-2 Typed override and match diagnostics** (planning session; the owner's G89 request; two independent designs,
  chosen design independently reviewed). The missing representation in G89-1 is the check's cause and compared values,
  not another message. Binding keeps these in its existing `OverrideFailure` dictionary; the adapters alone turn them
  into facts and Notes. Slot selection, signatures, condition proofs, match coverage and acceptance do not change.
  - `OverrideFailureCause` closes the existing nine causes. `NoBase` and `NoInheritedGroup` need no extra payload;
    `NoMatchingInputs` retains the first inherited function when one exists; `AmbiguousInputs` retains two candidates;
    `DuplicateSlot` retains the original slot and preceding implementation. `ExternalName` requires both compared names,
    the violating parameter's zero-based declaration index (including the receiver) and its name span. `ResultType`
    requires both compared bound Types and the written return Type when present. `OriginBinders` requires the original
    slot. `Condition` requires the original slot, condition node and the already computed `Unknown` or `Refuted` proof.
    Other payload fields are unused. Primary and related location selection stays unchanged; publication never re-proves.
  - `OverrideContractMismatch` publishes names as `expected:Text,actual:Text,cause:Enumeration,parameter:Number`, Types as
    `expected:Type,actual:Type,cause:Enumeration`, or Origin binders as `cause:Enumeration`, in that order. The actual
    parameter index makes the name schema distinct; the common `expected {0}, found {1}` Label applies to the first two.
    The Type schema uses existing `BoundPair` so both differing Type fragments survive elision. Other override codes
    publish `cause`; a condition also publishes the actual expression and proof. Explanation prose belongs only in Note.
  - Match publishes its existing `coverage` enumeration, with a numeric `case` only for `MissingCase` and
    `WholePayloadRequired`. Its four explanations stay in `Binding.Diagnostics.Match`; `MatchCoverage.Requirement`
    and the coverage judgment are unchanged. `Reason` strings, concatenated Type pairs and semantic `Describe` are gone.
  - Design A kept conversion in the phase adapters; independent B avoided redundant condition prose but put conversion
    in `DiagnosticOwner`. Chosen: A's owner and the nonredundant schemas. Rejected: keeping strings; equal-arity Type/Text
    alternatives (Type is Text plus its schema flag); a dummy discriminator; shared variant selection machinery;
    cause paraphrases disguised as condition facts; individual cause rendering in `DiagnosticOwner`. No new IR,
    failure code, table, component, migration exception or change to the shared diagnostic selector is needed.
    `VirtualDeclarations` and `BaseCalls` retain separate eligibility/use contracts and remain follow-up issues.
  - The change trades a larger value in the existing failure dictionary for direct typed data, removes the nine-argument
    recorder and combined-string conversion, and keeps warm failure Binding allocation-free. Fixed 128-failure
    cold/warm and retained-compilation measurements belong in `DiagnosticMeasurements`; evidence records the actual cost.
## Binding units (2026-10-18)

Units of the BU planning session (PLAN G129, G130 and the retention gap found by R4's E14 implementer), run in parallel with R4
and R5 on the owner's request of 2026-10-18; paused by R4-M77, resumed by R4-M78 and paused again by R4-M79 (all 2026-10-19), and
resumed by R4-M86 (2026-10-20).

- **BU-1** (2026-10-18; the BU planning session; correction of R4-M51's Stores clause, found by R4's E14 implementer at
  `f6b365bb`; R4-M51's contract stands) Stores of call retention (SPEC 15.6.4): an Origin occurrence is writable storage of
  its input when `RetentionWalk` has reached an invariant position through storage the call may write (an exclusive or raw
  referent, or an invariant position of a value the call may write, whose nominal Type may hide an exclusive layer) at or
  above it; every occurrence below that position is in it, past any layer, since a value stored there brings its whole
  Type. A shared layer or a non-exclusive pair layer stops the walk from reaching writable storage only before such a
  position (an rc payload held by value and a shared input's referent stay read only, SPEC 15.6.2, 5.2.1); a callable Type
  stores nothing. Why: rc and arc have no outer Origin, so the cut lost their payload's Origins (`Array<rc/S>.append`
  stored nothing, so A5 accepted writing `x` while the Array held `x@ref`), nor has a pair layer admitting only owning
  handles (`s is rc or arc`), so its concrete target had no R2 edge to the writable slot; a borrow layer's writable outer
  Origin, which its referent's Origins outlive (R2), hid the cut for borrows. Supersedes R4-M51's "not past a shared layer … nor past a
  non-exclusive pair layer" below a writable invariant position. Rejected: removing rc and arc from the shared layers (a
  case per form; it would also make an rc payload held by value writable); a store row per handle input. Not temporary.
- **BU-2** (2026-10-18; the BU planning session; PLAN G130, design B with its review's resolutions; the G130 entry, which its
  later units extend) Argument kinds (SPEC 10.5.1) have one owner, the canonical component `Binding.ArgumentKinds`: the kind of
  every argument part (a call argument and, recursively, an element of a Tuple or array literal argument, a written boundary
  of a mixed range and a payload of a contextual `.Case(...)`) is Literal, Composite, Waiting or Typed, and consumers read it
  through one query, `KindOf`; the component prepares a call's arguments and a Composite's parts and walks a Composite for
  slot evidence and for its fit to a candidate. It replaces `Binding.NestedCalls` and `Binding.ArrayArguments`.
  Representation: the kind a pass records for a part, keyed by syntax identity (`SourceRef`), replaces the Koto-keyed
  `waitingNestedCalls` set; the first unit records the nested calls the argument probe defers, and `KindOf` otherwise
  derives the kind from the part's syntax and binding state, as the consumers did. `SlotSolution` is the SPEC 10.8 solve
  state of one candidate (its Type, length and Origin slots and input Origins, scope, Self, declaring Type, explicit Type
  arguments, the fixed-construction flag and the Origin inference its evidence begins) with its own operations: an argument
  part's evidence, substitution of the solution and the judgment of the candidate's Constraints over it. It replaces the
  parallel arrays `TryCandidate` and its local evidence functions took; a Case construction is to supply its own data to it,
  with no branch on a missing function. Owner decisions (2026-10-18, in the BU planning session), implemented by G130's later
  units U2–U5: SPEC 10.5.1 is followed as written, so a contextual `.Case(...)` argument is Waiting and never probed per
  candidate, and a control-flow argument is Literal only when all its result sources are Literal; SPEC 10.2.1's Literal
  timing holds, so a Literal is no evidence during applicability and comparison and its default applies after selection,
  with the ambiguities that follow. Why: each consumer decided an argument's
  kind from syntax, and the element, payload and top-level paths decided it differently (PLAN G130). Rejected: fixing the
  walkers in place (design A's option (i), and fixes inside each walker: the dispatch copies and the two leaf rules for
  elements and top-level arguments stay); a Case construction as a synthesized constructor candidate through `BindCallCore`
  (design B's option (iii): a `FunctionKoto` per Case without syntax and HIR and MIR changes for a single-candidate solve); a
  Koto-keyed kind table (ARCH Code rules, Syntax identity). Open: a construction's unbound slot reports `MissingType`
  (`UnresolvedBinding_Kd`) while a call's reports `UnboundTypeArgument_Kd`. Not temporary.
  - U2, Literal timing (SPEC 10.2.1, 10.5.1; owner decision (2)): a Literal part is no evidence during applicability and
    comparison. At a position that holds an unbound slot it is checked only by the slot-free shape its default would have and
    leaves the slot unbound, so step 2 of 10.4 makes such candidates incomparable. For the selected candidate whose slot no
    evidence binds, `SolveSelected` applies the defaults to its Literal parts at positions that hold the slot (12.3; 4.6.2 rule 3,
    while rule 2, the other boundary's integer Type, stays range typing during candidate evaluation), records each as the part's
    fact (`ArgumentFact.Default`, keyed by `SourceRef`) and runs the candidate's checks once more. A failure is that candidate's
    own record and never reselects: a literal its default does not fit is its own `InvalidNumericLiteral_Kd`, a refuted
    Constraint keeps its fact. Under the argument probe a nested call or construction waits when another candidate is applicable
    or its result holds a Type or Semantics slot no evidence binds (a constructor's result holds all its slots; Origin slots
    never count). Arithmetic operands have their own probe (SPEC 13.3.4), which waits only on an ambiguity or a slot no default
    binds, so `identity(1) + identity(2)` stays typed. Gaps the timing exposed: a Contract argument holding an unbound slot leaves
    its clause unresolved instead of judging the callee's own reference; a pair's target projection `T` mentions its pair slot.
  - U3, one evidence walk and one fit walk (SPEC 10.5.1, 10.2, 10.8; owner decision (a) of PLAN G130): an element of a Tuple or
    array literal argument and a payload of a contextual Case are parameter positions. `PrepareArgument` prepares every part by
    its kind under the argument probe, which now covers elements, so a nested call there waits and a function name stays unbound
    for its position (`AtArgumentPosition`). `SlotSolution.InferArgument` is the one evidence dispatch for arguments and
    elements: a typed part through the common adaptation (a value read, erasure) and, at a Function pattern, its known call
    signature; an anonymous function's written header; a Never-typed part none, and a literal holding one no Type at a bare slot
    (D6). `FitArgument` is the one fit dispatch for call arguments, elements, contextual payloads and value calls
    (`ProbeValueCall`). A waiting element at an `F` of the candidate binds it (`WaitingBindsSlot`) and is completed with `F`'s
    signature after selection (`CompleteWaiting`), as a waiting argument is. Deleted: `InferAggregateCall`,
    `InferAggregateInputs`, `ProbeAggregateArgument`'s leaf and literal branches, `PrepareAggregateArgument`'s binding without
    expectation and `IndependentAggregateType`'s Never evidence. R11 is split (planning session, 2026-10-18): U3 lands its
    expected-result half, so an expected result Never is ordinary evidence (`let x: Never = identity(stop())` gives `T = Never`);
    the structural `Infer` skips a Never component until U5, whose commit removes the skip as it puts Case payloads on
    `InferArgument` (then `h(u)` with `u: (Never, i64)` gives `T = Never`, and `P.Pair(1, ((return 1), a))` and its swapped
    form give `T = i64`: U5's regression rows), since before U5 a Case payload bound whole would make its Never element
    evidence. Departure from the designs' expected record: `g((identity(true), a))` is `NoApplicableOverload_Kd` at `g`, not
    the inner call's error, because `identity(true)` is independently typable (`bool`) and that Type does not fit `i64`.
  - U4, control-flow arguments (SPEC 10.5.1, 14.9.1-14.9.2; owner decision (1), review R5): an `if`, `match`, `loop` or `do`
    part is Literal exactly when every result source is a literal, as ControlFlow's one source enumeration finds it
    (`SurveyResult`, the walk `FindResultEvidence` already makes, now also telling Never sources and fitting each literal
    source to a Type): it fits a candidate when every source does, takes its first literal source's default after selection
    and is completed at the decided Type. Literals beside only Never or unknown sources (`if c => 1 else => stop()`, `if c =>
    identity(1) else => 2`) need an expectation or a default, so the part waits. Any other control flow is bound under the
    argument probe, which reaches its result sources (`ResultTarget`, the inverse of the survey's sources); a source call
    that waits there makes the part wait (`if c => identity(1) else => identity(2)`). `KindOf` reads the recorded Literal or
    Waiting of an unbound part (`WasWaitingPart` replaces `WasWaitingNestedCall`). Arithmetic operands use the same
    predicate (`ResultSurvey.AllLiteral`), so a Never source no longer makes a right operand Literal: `x + (if c => 1 else
    => stop())` with `x: i64` is now `TypeMismatch_Kd`, as the left-operand form already was (accepted by the planning
    session with owner decision (1): SPEC 12.3.3 lets only literal-only expressions, never control flow, fit a provider's
    counterpart, 13.3.4, and 14.9.2 gives the `if` no candidate but its literal's default). Limit (open): the survey binds no
    source, so an unknown typed source beside literals makes the part wait rather than be typed (`keep(if c => foo.bar()
    else => 2)` leaves `T` unbound, where SPEC 14.9.2 gives `foo.bar()`'s Type); it goes with G129's late fit (BU decision
    E13: a join propagates its decided Type into its literal sources, after which such a part can be bound and is Typed).
  - U4b, the parts of a call that completes none (SPEC 23.1.2, 10.1; planning session): a Literal or waiting part is bound
    only once its call selects a candidate. A call that ends unresolved, with no selected candidate or one that failed before
    completing its arguments, binds each argument part still unbound on its own under the argument probe
    (`CompleteUnselected`, from `BindCall`), so the part's own problems are reported beside the call's record, once, and none
    that only the missing expectation causes: a Literal or waiting control-flow part's literal sources wait under the probe
    (`WaitsUnderProbe`) and its source calls defer, and the parts of a Tuple or array literal, a contextual Case and a
    waiting nested call are completed alike; a control-flow part already bound in the pass is not bound again. No candidate
    is selected again; anonymous functions stay under PLAN R1e. Rejected: binding the part before selection (a node bound
    in a pass is not bound again, so its literal sources would keep their defaults, and binding a `match` twice reports its
    arms as covered).
  - U5, Case construction on the walks (SPEC 6.5.2 item 2, 10.8.1, 10.5.1; design B section 5, D7, R1, R9, R11): the slots its
    qualifier and expected Type fix come first; a payload whose payload Type they settle is bound only at it, and every other
    payload is prepared as an argument is and is evidence by its kind through `SlotSolution.InferArgument`, which now serves a
    construction as data (the enum is binder and slot owner; `Binder`, `SlotOwner`, `OriginCount` and `Constructor` are fields,
    and only a candidate's operations read its `Function`). Under the argument probe a construction with an unbound slot waits
    (`takeOpt(Option.Some(1))`); otherwise the Literal defaults apply (`DefaultPayloads`) and are evidence; an unbound slot is
    the construction's own `MissingType` record (Q4 open), on which its waiting payloads depend (`MarkWaitingHeaders`; a part
    that still waits is no prerequisite its call consulted, so `let o = Option.Some(identity(1))` reports that root record).
    Each payload in source order then fits its decided payload Type (`FitArgument`; a misfit is the construction's
    `TypeMismatch_Kd`: `P.Pair(1, [a, a])`) and is completed there (`CompleteArgument`, G129's re-fit point, also used by the
    call path; `ErasePart`, the call path's erasure step) and adapted. Owner decision (1), R1: a contextual `.Case(...)` argument
    is Waiting and never probed per candidate, so `f(.Some(128))` over `Option<i8>` and `Option<i32>` is `AmbiguousBinding_Kd`.
    R11's at-depth half: `Infer` no longer skips a Never component (`h(u)` with `u: (Never, i64)` gives `T = Never`; a Never
    element is still no evidence, so `P.Pair(1, ((return 1), a))` gives `T = i64`). Deleted: the construction's three-pass
    loop and second adaptation loop, `PrepareContextualEnumInputs` and `ProbeContextualEnum`.
  - Completion (U6): G130 closes with U0 (SPEC 10.5.1 text), U1 (the component, behavior unchanged), U2 (Literal timing), U3
    (one evidence and one fit walk), U4 and U4b (control-flow arguments; the parts of a call that completes none) and U5 (Case
    construction; contextual Case waits). Rejected across the units: fixing each walker in place, a synthesized constructor
    candidate per Case, a Koto-keyed kind table, a temporary per-part evidence loop in the construction before U5, binding a
    Literal or waiting control-flow part before selection, and a second source walk for control flow. Open: a construction's
    unbound slot reports `MissingType` while a call's reports `UnboundTypeArgument_Kd` (above); the survey's limit (PLAN

- **BU-33 A macro publishes its selected call at the macro expression** (2026-10-24; the planning session after two independent
  designs and design review; G141) SPEC 17.4.2 and 22.5.1 make `$abort(message)` one Never call whose location is the macro expression,
  in a body, require failure, default or nested argument. Binding stored its plan on the inner invocation, but published that
  invocation as Call and the macro as Group; MIR recovered the location from the parent. Binding owns this publication contract.
  `CallPlan.Of` exposes the existing inner plan through its macro row, after the formatting-plan path (`$tryWrite`). The macro uses
  the existing Unary Call classification; its inner invocation is Covered Syntax, and the usual call operations acquire its arguments.
  - Inner storage stays for legacy ownership and lowering. No second plan, IR kind, table or state is introduced. Raw accessors retain
    their existing lifetime; current semantic queries revoke invalidated facts and a new Bind replaces the published facts. The macro
    view shares that same inner plan after rebind. This does not change Abort argument validation or the old lowering's source handling.
  - Removes the macro Group classification and acquisition, the formatting-only Covered condition and MIR's Abort parent correction.
    Rejected: moving or copying storage to the macro (breaks legacy readers or duplicates the decision), adding a source field to
    CallPlan (extra state while retaining the redundant Group), or a new IR/table. The existing view row corrects the public subject
    without another allocation; removing Group work is expected to preserve compilation and native costs.

- **BU-55 Binding's walks over a shared Type part decide each distinct part once per query: BU-19's table for the answer and
  existence walks, the atom walk's positions, a container frame's Tuples** (2026-10-30; PLAN G243's O1 to O3, unit bu69; the BU
  planning session's answers of 2026-10-30 to bu69's questions: O2's key (a′), and the Origin-free family as the unit's scope) SPEC
  3.8, R4's V16: a walk's work is linear in the distinct parts of an interned Type, not in the paths to them.
  - Census (O3). A Roslyn call-graph pass over `src/Kimi/Compiler/Binding` found 974 recursive members and 155 SCCs that descend into
    a Type's parts; every recursive member got a visit counter. The probe is R4's V16 family `D_i<T> { x: D_{i+1}<(T, T)> }` through
    Tuples, a Tuple of two fixed arrays, enum payloads, Option, a struct with two Fields of one Type, rc handles and raw leaves, used
    through a member path, a generic callee at D_n, `==`, `T is Copy` and a called closure capturing the Tuple tree, at n = 16, 20
    and 24 over Bind, every call's retention and BuildMir. Eight walks grew as 2^n; their visits at n = 20, before and after, on the
    same program: RetentionWalk/RetentionParts 9,437,236 and 374, VisitInlineLayout 2,097,514 and 784, CompleteProjections 6,293,913
    and 7,684, ProveTypeLengths 8,389,879 and 1,422, CheckTypeConstraints (CheckTypeOriginRelations once per visit) 17,832,428 and
    10,935, ComparisonProof 1,048,575 and 40, DependentType 1,048,982 and 428, HasUnsubstitutedInput 1,048,589 and 11. Bind fell from
    3.8 s to 0.9 s and the retentions from 0.87 s to 0.04 s, both flat in n afterwards. Every other walk stays polynomial on the
    family.
  - Cause, shared by all eight: a part reached along many paths is walked as a tree, with neither a table nor an exact gate. BU-19 had
    named seven of them as open adopters ("in the unit whose reproducer first reaches it").
  - Answer walks adopt BU-19's `TypeMemo`, each entry call a query:
    - `CompleteProjections` (`completedParts`, through `CompletedPart`; the declaration fixed).
    - `CheckTypeConstraints` (`formedParts`, through `FormedPart`). A part's answer is its proof and the cause it rests on; a part met
      again reads both into its own proof scope (`ReadVerdict`), so `EndProof` gives what a recomputation gives. `EndProof`'s cause
      rule is `ProofCause`, shared.
    - `ComparisonProof` (`comparedParts`, composite parts; contract, scope and operators fixed).
    - Only a component with components (and a query's root, `ComparisonPlans`) is recorded, never a leaf (cheaper to answer again
      than to record, as `FirstVisit` rules). Recording every part cost about 91 KB of cold Bind bytes on Hello; recording only
      those components costs about 21 KB.
  - Existence walks share `visitedParts` through `FirstVisit`: `ProveTypeLengths` and `DependentType`. `DependentType` becomes an
    instance member that walks through a local function, keeping its parameters; `DependentConstraint` and `IsDependentConstraint`
    follow. `HasUnsubstitutedInput` takes BU-19's exact gate: a part carrying no Origin (`CarriesOrigin`) names none.
  - O1, `RetentionWalk`. What a position adds depends on its Type, `at`, `variance` and `callable` alone, the scope, raw inputs and
    raw visits being fixed for a contract or an erased signature. A second visit appends the same atoms again, so each such position
    is walked once (`retentionPositions`, cleared with `retentionRawVisits`): the atom list loses duplicates only, which change no
    node, edge or row. bu36's candidate key.
  - O2, `VisitInlineLayout` (superseded by BU-65, which replaces the walk). A visit's effect depends on the Type and the
    container stack. Each container frame (the root and each pushed struct or enum instance) is one query of `layoutParts`, whose
    stack is fixed. A Tuple or fixed array whose visit closed no
    cycle is not visited again in its frame. Every struct or enum instance below it is then finite (skipped) or meets a container on
    the same stack, which adds nothing again, so the skipped revisit is a no-op under dev's rule. `finiteInlineLayouts` is unchanged.
  - Rejected:
    - (a), any part met again in a frame skipped. It changes a verdict: dev marks a struct finite when its visit adds no new cycle
      member, so in `struct A {p: (M, M)}; struct R2<T> {m: M}; struct M {r: R2<i32>}` the second M marks M finite and R2 goes
      unreported; (a) would report R2.
    - (b), a global Tuple memo. It would miss C in `struct R {r: C<u8>}; struct C<T> {t: (C<i32>, u8)}`, whose Tuple first closes
      nothing under R's stack.
    - (c), a declaration-level cycle graph: a redesign (taken by BU-65: G310's exactness needs it).
    - BU-35's (b), one shared walker.
  - Evidence:
    - The probe's every call's and function's retention, Bind's records and BuildMir's counts are identical before and after for
      the tuple, raw, array, enum and two-Field forms at n = 16 and 20 and the `ref` form at n = 12, 16 and 20.
    - The diagnostic snapshot and the registered mir ledger show no difference.
    - Tests: TypeDagScalingTest `InstanceChainWalksAreLinearInDistinctParts` (tuple, array, enum and raw rows at n = 40, so a walk
      that re-visits shared parts meets 2^40 paths). It hangs on dev; undoing any one of the eight fixes alone hangs it again.
      InlineLayoutTest's rows pin the two forms above at dev's verdicts.
    - Cost (the review's run: pinned, full JIT, one folder, interleaved, A/A ≤ 0.2%): cold Bind time +1.3% to +2.4% on Hello and
      +0.8% on Milestone 27, BuildMir equal; cold Bind bytes +21 KB to +27 KB and BuildMir +12 KB (the tables' capacity); retained
      +19 KB / +22 KB; warm Bind 0 B.
  - Open (PLAN G309, G310):
    - The Origin-carrying family (`D1<ref/i32 during a>`) reaches about twenty more exponential Binding walks. Among them is
      ContractType, whose table BU-19 rejected for its path-dependent `normalizingAssociated` guard.
    - BuildMir's own walks over these shapes are exponential (R5's W1 and R4's W2); W3, TyCtxt.Retains for A5, is O1's and closed.
    - Inline-cycle diagnostics depend on declaration order and duplicated parts, as in (a)'s example (pinned), and
      `struct R {r: C<i32>}; struct C<T> {t: (C<i32>, u8)}` is accepted with no InvalidInlineLayout_Kd (on dev too; G310).

- **BU-56 A declaration's written Origin that names a body local's written Type and selects a body local's atom is a located
  `Unsupported_Kd`, an interim for wrong code until PLAN G230's (A)** (2026-10-30; PLAN G230, BU's unit bu70: option (B) of its
  stopped design, the planning session's decision, R4 agreeing; fix round 1 after review 1) SPEC 15.3.4, 23.1.1, 23.1.2.
  - SPEC reading: a named nested function's signature may name visible Origins of enclosing functions, each a fixed Origin of it, and a
    local set is visible in the following scope, so SPEC decides the forms: d6 (a store of `put`'s own input through `during x.s` of an
    enclosing `var w: W{x}`) is Unproven at the input, as d6b (an enclosing parameter's Origin) is; d6v (a store `during x.s` of an
    input `during x.s`) and d6r (a read) are valid. No Language error.
  - Cause: a nested header is its declaration's, bound with no body before the body binds the local (R4-M101 E1, E3), so `x.s`, `w.s`
    or `r` read the local's annotation, whose omitted Origins are atoms formed outside every body (E5's broken-contract class) that
    nothing links to the local's region: the store was accepted on both pipelines (d6 ran `leak 41`; d6c passed `check` and failed
    LLVM generation). A root function naming a document-local is the same form (`leak 41` under MIR code generation). An unannotated
    local has no Type yet there; the header fails, and `BindFunction` binds it again in the body, which has typed the local (d6u,
    `LocalRegionCompletionTest`'s NestedNamedFinite). The interim leaves that class: every probe of it is sound, but its invalid twins
    get misplaced records (`CallActivationConflict_Kd` in `put`, `ComparisonLoanConflict_Kd` at a block's local), a valid
    `pick(r)` of `func pick(v: ref/i32 during r) -> ref/i32 during r` is `NoApplicableOverload_Kd`, and the MIR build (shadow)
    reports d6u's local region in `put`'s declaration row as `InternalInvariant_Kd` (E2's broken contract; the ledger's (b) rows
    `b-g230-e2`): (A) removes them.
  - Rule: `Binding.OriginCandidate`, where a written Origin's name resolves, records the located `Unsupported_Kd` at the written Origin
    (`UnlinkedLocalType`) when the name is a body local's set or annotated value, the Origin (a name or projection) is bound with no
    body outside a local's own declaration, and the Origin the name selects (`SelectedOrigin`, shared with `BindOriginName` and the
    projection: a borrow's outer Origin, a declared slot) is a body local's atom; the name resolves to nothing, so no relation, row or
    call judges it and its dependents rest on it. It decides by the name, so it holds where `BindFunction` binds the header again and
    the Type has become the local's region. A name that selects no Origin keeps its Language error (`during w` of a non-borrow `w`,
    SPEC 15.2.1, and an absent slot `w.zz` or `x.zz`: `InvalidOriginBinding_Kd`); one that selects a parameter's or a contract's is
    judged (d6b; `let r: ref/i32 during a`; `r.s` of `r: ref/W during a`, whose slot the body completes from `a`: dev accepted its
    store, now Unknown at the input). One rule for every declaration form (a parameter's or result's Type, a Type argument's `during`,
    a clause, a root function's signature). A Closure header, bound in its evaluating body, keeps BU-28's `EnclosingAtom`; SPEC 15.3.4's
    `pass` is accepted. Valid forms are `Unsupported_Kd` (d6v, d6r; STATUS Origins).
  - Removal condition: (A) lands, with R4 (R4-M101 is R4's): a recorded declaring body of a named nested function (bound in
    `BindFunction` beside `BoundClosure.EvaluatingBody`; Binding.ExecutableBodies.cs forbids deriving it from syntax) extending
    `EnclosingAtom`'s chain, the name link (a nested header's local name resolving through the local's declaration, or nested headers
    bound after the local, changing E3) and E2's declaration-row reading of an enclosing body's atom under the signature's
    well-formedness premise. Then this rule, its rows and `b-g230-e2` go: d6 is Unproven at its input, d6v and d6r are accepted.
  - Rejected: (A) now (the design's prototype: the chain alone changes nothing; the link alone judges w's region as `put`'s; both
    make every form Unproven at the parameter, and admitting body atoms as declaration-row atoms loops in `check` on d6); testing
    the resolved atom alone (where `BindFunction` binds the header again the name finds the local's region, so the U did not stick
    and d6 fell into the unannotated class); every local's name (moves NestedNamedFinite, a valid native fixture, and d6u); testing
    every Origin of the local's Type before the name selects one (review 1, B1: invalid names became `Unsupported_Kd`).
  - Tests: `ClosureEnvironmentOriginTest`: d6, d6c, d6w, d6r2, d6v, d6r, a clause `origin q == x.s` and the root form fail before,
    and so does the store through `r.s` (Unknown); d6b, a local annotated with a parameter's Origin, d6u, `pass`, the three invalid
    names and the Closure twins (BU-28's Unproven store, a valid read) are unchanged.

  over a written Type decide each distinct part once per call** (2026-10-30; the BU planning session after G307's joint design: BU's

    Type the part's declaration writes at the positions (as for RawStep: a struct's root is [], an enum's positions start at the
    payload), followed through Tuples and fixed arrays, while it is a Tuple, a fixed array or a raw layer (BU-35's `written`, one
    private `Written` that the hold walk reads too); null at or past a Type parameter, a pair layer, a nominal or an open projection,
    where no declaration writes the part, and at an enum's []. It reads the declaration only, in O(|p|), total, 0 B warm.
  - Invariants from a part's first positions (a struct's [], a Case's [i]): monotone (null at p is null at p·s); at a raw layer it is

    W (Own needs W). BU's review 2 measured it over 13 classes and its probes, legacy and mir: W equals `declared` at all 175,969
    StoredStep and StoredMembers calls and is monotone; 0 conflicts for (K, W, I) over 175,525 keys and for K alone below the region
    (649 keys); dropping I conflicts 72 times (a conditional slot's case) and dropping W once (a twin).
  - A view and not a bool: a closed projection's resolution is what a declaration writes, so `x: Dup<…Dup<L>.Item…>.Item` with
